source.citation: Unsigned review of Berndt, Archiv für klinische Chirurgie (1896), no. 4, in Medical Record 50 (August 8, 1896): 198–199. Second of Berndt's two cases.
source.place: Germany (reported in a New York journal)

complaints: swelling of the neck; eyes protruding
presentation.course: Palpitation began at 25 after hard work. Always irritable. Neck swelling appeared about two years later, then darkened skin and protruding eyes. Ten years of medical treatment without benefit.
presentation.priorTreatment: Ten years of unspecified medical treatment, without effect.

findings: both thyroid lobes enlarged, the left more; a nodule behind the breastbone
periodDiagnosis: exophthalmic goitre (Graves' or Basedow's disease), then often called a neurosis

treatments.response: greatly improved; the operation was cut short by heart failure, and she died of pneumonia after influenza a year later

outcome: Improved after surgery; died a year later of pneumonia.
quotes: palpitation of the heart developed at the age of twenty-five years in the train of hard work
Berndt looks upon exophthalmic goitre as a reflex neurosis

modernReading.text: Graves' disease (hyperthyroidism). The fear, sleeplessness, palpitation, and irritability come from excess thyroid hormone, not from nerves. A doctor in 1896 could find the goitre, the eyes, and a rapid pulse.

constrained.rule: mostly female (Oppenheimer, JNMD 22 (1895): 216, passage 3977283, estimates about twelve women to one man)
protrusion may be absent early; the seed decides

notes: Valuable because it looks like a nervous complaint and is not. A New York or American case of the same condition would be a better source; this one is a German report reviewed in the Medical Record.
